record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.context_brief: Borel-type conjecture for Poincaré duality groups
record.original_question: Let π be a Poincaré duality group, meaning that the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(π,1) satisfies Poincaré duality with respect to a fundamental class in H^n(K(π,1); Z) for some n. Is K(π,1) simple-homotopy equivalent to a closed topological manifold, and if so is that manifold unique up to homeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Let π be a Poincare duality group. That is, the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(π,1) satisfies Poincare duality with respect to a fundamental class in H^n(K;Z) for some n. Prove or disprove the "Borel conjecture": K(π,1) is simple homotopy equivalent to a closed, topological m-manifold which is unique up to homeomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A discrete group $\pi$ is called an $n$-dimensional Poincaré duality group if its Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(\pi,1)$ (an aspherical CW complex with fundamental group $\pi$) satisfies Poincaré duality of formal dimension $n$ with respect to a fundamental class in $H^n(K(\pi,1);\mathbb{Z})$ (in either the orientable or twisted sense). 

Prove or disprove the following Borel-type conjecture: For every Poincaré duality group $\pi$ of dimension $n$, the space $K(\pi,1)$ is simple-homotopy equivalent to a closed topological $n$-manifold, and any two such closed topological manifolds simple-homotopy equivalent to $K(\pi,1)$ are homeomorphic.
artifact.status_search_result: The Borel conjecture for Poincaré duality groups remains open in general. It has been established in important special cases—most notably by Farrell–Jones for fundamental groups of nonpositively curved closed manifolds, and by Bartels–Lück for hyperbolic and CAT(0) groups—but the existence question (whether every Poincaré duality group is the fundamental group of an aspherical closed topological manifold) and the full uniqueness statement remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Aspherical manifolds - Manifold Atlas
status_evidence.snippet: A finitely presented group is a d-dimensional Poincaré duality group iff it is the fundamental group of an aspherical closed d-dimensional topological manifold (conjecturally).
status_evidence.claim: The existence half of the conjecture for Poincaré duality groups remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The Borel Conjecture for hyperbolic and CAT(0)-groups
status_evidence.snippet: Bartels–Lück prove the Borel conjecture in dimensions ≥ 5 for hyperbolic and CAT(0) groups.
status_evidence.claim: Important partial results exist but the general conjecture is still open.

status_evidence.title: The Borel Conjecture for manifolds with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate variants of the Borel conjecture, indicating that the general statement is still under active study.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still actively studied, not resolved.
